title.narrative: Integrated Health and WASH Response to the Cholera Outbreak in Yilmana Densa District, Amhara Region

description.narrative: ltpgtSince the cholera outbreak began on January 2, 2025, cases have surged across 45 woredas in Amhara, reaching 6,050 reported cases and 79 deaths—an alarming 1.31% case fatality rate (Source: Amhara Public Health Institute). The hardest-hit districts—Bahir Dar Zuria, Bahir Dar City, and Jawi—face critical transmission risks due to inadequate WASH infrastructure, poor hygiene practices, and reliance on contaminated water sources. Pilgrim mobility and worsening security conditions have further exacerbated the outbreak, with holy water sites like Andasa and Abuna Hara serving as transmission hotspots. Humanitarian response efforts have been severely constrained due to ongoing armed conflicts and displacement (OCHA, WHO).ltbrgtIn response, Health Development and Anti-Malaria Association (HDAMA) is launching a 6-month emergency cholera intervention from June 2025 to January 2026, targeting Yilmana Densa district. This $169,999.98 initiative aims to reach 100,000 individuals, including 12,000 pilgrims, with an integrated Health, WASH, and Risk Communication and Community Engagement (RCCE) approach. The primary goal is to reduce the case fatality rate to below 1% among an anticipated caseload of 10,000.ltbrgtThe Health component will enhance cholera case management by training 50 local healthcare workers in critical areas such as IPC and the operation of CTCs and ORPs. CTCs and health posts will be equipped with ORS, RL solution, and essential antibiotics. Additionally, vaccination and sensitization campaigns will educate 50,000 people on prevention and available services.ltbrgtThe WASH component will improve access to safe water by installing two 20,000-liter storage tanks, rehabilitating two wells and natural springs, and constructing sanitation facilities—including constructing two communal latrines and two shower rooms at the selected holy water sites. WASH NFIs such as soap and jerrycans will be distributed to 68,800 beneficiaries, and 30 health workers will be trained in IPC measures..ltbrgtThe RCCE strategy will engage 14,000 individuals (70% of the target population) through billboards, leaflets, media broadcasts, and mobile van outreach. Advocacy meetings with local leaders and religious figures will strengthen community ownership of cholera prevention measures.ltbrgtThe project will mainstream protection to support vulnerable populations, ensuring access to MHPSS and GBV prevention services for at least 7,200 pilgrims. Project staff and volunteers will receive orientation on GBV and disability inclusion.ltbrgtKey cross-cutting activities include regular joint field assessments, equipment procurement, coordination with the Amhara Health Bureau, WHO, and religious leaders, and a strong focus on gender sensitivity and disability inclusion. The project aims to reduce cholera cases by 75%, ensure 100% functionality of rehabilitated WASH facilities, increase cholera prevention awareness among 70% of the population, and provide timely protection services to 60% of identified vulnerable groups.ltbrgtlt/pgt
